battlefield.note: An open plain levelled for chariots, the Bumodus river with two fords on the west and the hills of Jebel Maqlub in the north-east.

popup.title: Gaugamela: Alexander Charges
popup.body:
You command Alexander's army on the plain that Darius levelled for his scythed chariots. Your phalanx can stand against the chariots; your javelinmen and archers can break them. The Persian line is longer than yours: wait for it to stretch and swing onto your left, then drive the Companion cavalry through the gap to Darius's camp.

Objective: Capture Darius's camp.

At Gaugamela in 331 BCE Alexander the Great beat a much larger Persian army under Darius III. When the Persian left followed his move to the right, a gap opened and Alexander charged through it toward Darius, who fled.

popup.title: The scythed chariots
popup.body: Darius sends his scythed chariots at your phalanx. Meet them with the javelinmen and archers, and let the phalanx stand.

popup.title: Bessus rides around the flank
popup.body: The Bactrian horse is swinging wide around your right. Hold them off with part of your force; the Persian line is stretching to follow.

popup.title: The gap opens
popup.body: The whole Persian line is swinging onto Parmenion and the Bumodus ford, and the centre in front of Darius's camp is opening. Hold the ford with the left wing and charge the gap with the Companions.

popup.title: The Greek allies
popup.body: The allied Greek infantry of the second line comes up behind the phalanx.

popup.title: The King's Kinsmen
popup.body: Darius's guard gathers at the camp for a last stand.
